title_en: Wonders of Chinese Engineering (13/20): The Ping An Finance Center
note_en: 曾 (céng) marks something that was true at some point in the past but may not be now: 建成时曾是中国第二高、世界第四高的建筑 "when it was finished, it was once the second-tallest building in China and the fourth-tallest in the world." English gets this meaning from "once" or "used to," but Chinese has no past tense, so 曾 (or 曾经) does the work; the text uses it again in 施工方曾因担心…而暂停施工 "construction was once halted over concerns that…."

sentences.en: At this point Layla closed her laptop and thought: under the original design, with a 60-meter antenna on top, the tower should have reached 660 meters and beaten the Shanghai Tower, but concerns about flight safety killed the antenna plan, and the final height was only 599.1 meters. As a result, when it was completed the tower ranked only fourth in the world, behind the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, the Shanghai Tower, and the Abraj Al-Bait Clock Tower in her hometown of Mecca. She couldn't help thinking that height rankings are always changing, and that what really matters about a tower may not be where it ranks, but what it means to the people who live around it.
